Question_text: Walt owns a company which has developed a new computer game for adults. A focus group report shows customers like it. Walt has been considering the marketing mix, including the packaging for this product which is likely to be sold in many countries. ‘I don't want to use a wholesaler as it would affect my profit margin' he said.
Sub_topic: Primary methods: postal questionnaire, online survey, interviews, focus groups
Importance: reward for risk, finance source
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct
Forms: advertising, sales promotion, influence on sales
Use of internet, social media for promotion

Parts.part_text: What is meant by a 'focus group'?
Identify two reasons why packaging might be important for the new computer game.
Explain why the profit margin might be important for Walt's business.
Identify and explain two advantages to Walt if he decided to use a wholesaler to distribute his products.
Consider two possible methods of promotion that Walt could use for the new game. Recommend which method he should use. Justify your answer.

Question_text: CLW makes wood furniture, including chairs and tables. Demand has risen quickly over the past 3 years and the business needs to increase the scale of production at its factory. The factory is located near the city centre in an area of low unemployment. The Finance Director has produced a business plan, including a balance sheet. The Finance Director is pleased with CLW's liquidity. Question_text: NCE manufactures cars in 4 factories using flow production. NCE's Human Resources Director thinks good induction training helps achieve high productivity. Factory X is its most efficient factory. Last year the size of the new car market fell by 20%. NCE now has to make 400 workers redundant at one of its other factories. 'I am pleased NCE is a large business', said the HR Director, 'I think a small business cannot survive in this competitive market.’ Table 2: NCE operations data for 2014 Number of cars made 168000 Number of employees 2800

Importance of training to business, employees
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Causes of failure: management skills, environment changes, liquidity

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'flow production'?
Calculate the output per employee in 2014.

Question_text: Nellis is a public limited company. It specialises in building large luxury houses. Over the past 3 years its profits have increased as the country is experiencing an economic boom. 'It's not all good news the Government has announced plans to increase interest rates and introduce new legal controls to protect the environment' said the Managing Director. He believes these new legal controls to protect the environment will only make businesses (such as Nellis) less profitable.
Unit: UNIT 6: External influences on business activity
Sub_topic: Stages of business cycle: growth, boom, recession, slump
Business impact on environment: global warming

Parts.part_text: What is meant by an 'economic boom'?
Identify two stages (other than boom) of the business cycle.
Explain how a rise in interest rates might affect Nellis.
Identify two stakeholder groups. Explain why each group is important to this business.
The Managing Director believes that the new legal controls to protect the environment will only make businesses (such as Nellis) less profitable. Do you agree? Justify your answer.
